_comment: Interactions: how one option changes what another does.
This file holds the ones that are a READING of a sentence. The ones that are a column are
derived instead, in build/src/interactions.rs: `regex.tsv.reachable` already says
`requires -P` on 25 rows and `default-only` on one, so those 26 engine preconditions are
machine-derived and cannot drift from the index that states them.
What is left is prose. `unreachable.tsv` says of the two size-limit flags: 'Both flags bound
the default engine only. Under -P they do not constrain PCRE2 at all.' That is an interaction,
but turning it into atoms is a judgement, so it is written here where it can be reviewed as
one rather than buried in a parser.
A predicate is disjunctive normal form: `terms` is a list of disjuncts, each a list of atoms
ANDed together. `[[a, b], [c]]` means `(a AND b) OR c`. There is no nesting, and if some
interaction genuinely needs it the answer is a new interaction referencing this one, not an
An interaction naming a mechanism this catalog does not hold, an operator nobody defined, or
an assertion that does not exist is a BUILD ERROR. An unresolvable evidence handle reads
exactly like evidence, which is why it is checked rather than trusted.

interactions.effect: Bounds the default Rust regex engine only. Under -P it does not constrain PCRE2 at all, so a pattern that would have been rejected as too large is instead handed to an engine this flag cannot bound.
Bounds the default Rust regex engine's DFA cache only. Under -P it does not constrain PCRE2, which has its own limits reachable through in-pattern verbs rather than through this flag.

Selects PCRE2 in place of the default Rust regex engine. This changes which constructs are available in both directions: lookaround and backreferences become usable, and the linear-time guarantee is given up.
Disables Unicode mode, which changes what character classes and word boundaries match rather than merely how fast they run. A result set that differs under this flag is not a bug in either run.
A pattern spanning a line boundary matches nothing without this flag, because ripgrep searches line by line unless told otherwise. The absence of matches is not the absence of occurrences.

ast-grep consumes the file set a prior ripgrep pass produced. The composition is recall-preserving only when the literal ripgrep matched on is implied by the structural pattern; otherwise the narrowing can drop files the pattern would have matched.
